title: A Visitor for the Hymn
premise: Folklorist Isandro Vane has spent three years in the isolated village of Hallowmere, recording hymns the villagers will sing once but never repeat, and telling herself the nocturnal noises are pipes, wind, bad wiring. When her sleep-recording equipment captures a second voice answering her half-spoken questions with unnerving accuracy, she realizes the village's founders bound something beneath the chapel that feeds on sung memory—and her recordings have been feeding it hers. As the harvest moon approaches and villagers begin forgetting their own children, Isandro discovers the founders' ritual was left deliberately unfinished: a hymn requiring a voice from outside the bloodline to complete it. She must choose between finishing the ritual—which will erase every song, and every memory of her, from the world—or letting the thing rise. In the end she sings the final verse alone in the flooded crypt, sacrificing her three years of collected memory; the village forgets her entirely, and the last chapter is told through a stranger who finds a tape labeled in handwriting no one recognizes.
about_author: Odile Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist of regional folk music collections who spent a decade cataloguing songs whose origins could not be verified. They write horror about what survives when communities decide what to remember.

chapters.title: The Song They Sing Once
chapters.summary: Isandro records the harvest hymn at the chapel, noting how the congregation's voices flatten on the third verse and how old Marta Voss refuses to repeat a single line afterward. Third-person limited, Isandro's POV. The beat is quiet unease—the reader senses rules Isandro hasn't learned yet.

chapters.title: Three Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: A flashback-structured chapter reviewing Isandro's rationalizations for the noises: the dragging above her ceiling, the wet footsteps, the humming in the well. Her editor's emails press her to finish the book and leave. First person, Isandro's POV. The emotional beat is self-deception beginning to crack.

chapters.title: What Answers at Night
chapters.summary: Isandro leaves recorders running while she sleeps and wakes to find a second voice on the audio—low, patient—answering questions she only thought aloud. It knows her mother's lullaby. First person POV. The beat shifts from skepticism to dread as the evidence becomes undeniable.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: In the parish archive, Isandro finds the founders' ledger describing a binding 'sung shut' beneath the chapel in 1847, with the final verse left blank by design. Marta catches her reading and warns her: outsiders who learn the verses don't leave. Third person limited. Beat: the stakes widen beyond Isandro.

chapters.title: Children of the Forgetting
chapters.summary: Villagers begin losing memories—the baker can't recall his daughter's face; the schoolteacher teaches a class list with names missing. Isandro realizes her recordings correlate with each loss. First person POV. The beat is guilt: her curiosity has been spending other people's pasts.

chapters.title: Marta's Confession
chapters.summary: Dying Marta Voss reveals she was meant to be the completing voice fifty years ago and fled, leaving the binding frayed ever since. She gives Isandro the founders' notation and begs her to finish what she couldn't. Third person limited, alternating briefly into Marta's memory. Beat: grief and inherited cowardice.

chapters.title: The Voice Wears a Face
chapters.summary: The entity escalates, appearing in reflections and borrowed shapes—including Isandro's own—offering her a bargain: leave now, keep your memories, let the village pay. First person POV. The beat is temptation; power offered freely is its own corruption.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for the End
chapters.summary: Isandro recruits the few villagers still whole to learn the hymn's true verses, rehearsing in the chapel as the thing unravels the building around them—one singer flees mid-verse and is unmade into silence. Third person limited. Beat: terror fused with resolve.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon, Flooded Crypt
chapters.summary: On the night of the moon, Isandro descends alone into the waterlogged crypt where the founders' bones hold the binding's root, and begins the final verse as the entity floods her mind with everything she's recorded. Climax, first person POV. Beat: sacrifice chosen knowingly.

chapters.title: A Tape No One Remembers
chapters.summary: Epilogue from the POV of an archivist visiting Hallowmere years later: the village is peaceful, no one recalls any folklorist, and a stranger's tape plays a hymn ending on a verse no local has ever heard. Third person limited. Beat: haunting resolution—the price of survival is being survived without trace.
